question: is there a weight at which delivery becomes risky?

sources.title: Good Health Before Pregnancy: Prepregnancy Care | ACOG

text: Your doctor makes the medical call. There isn’t one single weight number where delivery suddenly becomes risky. ACOG says body size is usually assessed with BMI, not weight alone, and weight gain guidance depends on pre-pregnancy BMI [1][2]. ACOG also says estimated fetal weight can be inaccurate, so “big baby” estimates are not exact [2].

sources.title: Maternal Obesity and Occurrence of Fetal Macrosomia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis - PMC

text: Your doctor makes the medical call. In simple words: bigger maternal weight is linked with a higher chance of a very large baby [1]. But lower weight gain is not simply “better,” because it can also raise the chance of a baby being too small [1]. For suspected big baby, NICE says the choices are waiting, induction, or caesarean, and the evidence is uncertain overall .
